definitions.explanation: The son of one's sibling. Used for both the son of a brother and the son of a sister.

examples.japanese: {甥|おい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦{小学校|しょうがっこう}→小学校：01055_shougakkou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入学|にゅうがく}する→入学する：01851_nyuugakusuru⟧。
examples.english: My nephew will start elementary school this year.

examples.japanese: ⟦{甥|おい}っ{子|こ}→甥っ子：30760_oikko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大|おお}きく→大きい：00335_ookii⟧⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧、⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧⟦{高校生|こうこうせい}→高校生：01580_koukousei⟧になった。
examples.english: My nephew has grown up and is already a high school student.

notes:
USAGE:
When referring to one's own nephew in polite conversation, use {甥|おい} or the more casual ⟦{甥|おい}っ{子|こ}→甥っ子：30760_oikko⟧. When referring to someone else's nephew politely, use {甥御|おいご}さん.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{姪|めい}→姪：03899_mei⟧: niece
- ⟦{甥|おい}っ{子|こ}→甥っ子：30760_oikko⟧: nephew (casual, affectionate)
- {甥御|おいご}さん: someone else's nephew (polite)

WRITING:
The kanji {甥|おい} is a single-kanji word. Also sometimes written ⟦{甥|おい}っ{子|こ}→甥っ子：30760_oikko⟧ in casual speech, which adds a diminutive, affectionate nuance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{甥|おい}っ{子|こ}→甥っ子：30760_oikko⟧: nephew (casual)
- {甥御|おいご}さん: nephew (polite, about others' nephews)
- {甥|おい}{姪|めい}: nephews and nieces
